findings.statement: This is a standalone precondition check
findings.evidence: `git -C LANE show BASE:tools/mutate-and-run.sh | grep -n 'repeat'` -> no output: the runner has no repeat-control option, and the gate is its own tool (tools/repeat-control.py). corpus/knowledge/repeated-control-precondition.md:70 makes the same call: 'A repeat-control run is a precondition observation, not a mutation leg'. So the gate is a standalone precondition instrument, and the check does not modify the runner (the false part of the sentence is only the stale 'six-leg' descriptor, reported first).

findings.statement: | Three or more zero-exit controls match on raw stdout and stderr | `controls_match` | Only this finite sample matched; not a determinism proof |
findings.evidence: argv ['python3','tools/repeat-control.py','--runs','3','--out',DIR,'--','true'] -> `REPEAT_RUN 1 exit=0`, `REPEAT_RUN 2 exit=0`, `REPEAT_RUN 3 exit=0`, `REPEAT_COMPARE identical=yes runs=3`, `REPEAT_CONTROL: controls_match`, exit=0; bytes are compared unnormalized (tools/repeat-control.py:22-24). The 'three or more' floor is enforced: argv [...,'--runs','2',...] -> stderr `repeat-control: --runs must be >= 3, got 2`, `REPEAT_CONTROL: invalid_usage`, exit=64. The bound matches the tool's own limitation text at :92-94 ('N finite observations agreed on this host in this environment — it is not a determinism proof and it cures no flakiness'); the row omits the host/environment scope there, a weaker paraphrase rather than a false claim. Receipts: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt, selftest.txt.

findings.statement: | Equal nonzero controls, or command unavailable | Could not evaluate baseline | No mutation kill-rate claim |
findings.evidence: argv [...,'--','sh','-c','echo same; exit 7'] -> `REPEAT_RUN 1 exit=7`, `REPEAT_RUN 2 exit=7`, `REPEAT_RUN 3 exit=7`, `REPEAT_COMPARE identical=yes runs=3`, `REPEAT_CONTROL: baseline_nonzero`, exit=2; argv [...,'--','/nonexistent-cmd-xyz'] -> `REPEAT_RUN 1 exit=unavailable` (x3), `REPEAT_CONTROL: command_unavailable`, exit=2. EXIT_BY_ID (tools/repeat-control.py:122-130) maps both ids to 2, and both are could-not-evaluate classes, so 'Could not evaluate baseline' / 'No mutation kill-rate claim' holds. Note for the integrator: the decision cell is prose, not a string the tool prints; the printed ids are `baseline_nonzero` and `command_unavailable` (independently observed by T49ExecR12Cmd M2), so a cold reader cannot map the cell to a receipt line. Receipts: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt, probe-findings/nonzero.finding.txt, probe-findings/unavail.finding.txt.

The gate exists because one control run cannot separate a stable baseline from a flaky one: tools/repeat-control.py:4-10 ('The mutation runner checks the pristine control exactly once per sweep ... one run cannot separate a stable baseline from a flaky one'); S004 requires that the tree first pass reliably (corpus/SOURCES.md:15 'tests must first pass reliably in a copied tree').

findings.statement: put evidence outside any tree it inspects
findings.evidence: Stated by the tool itself: tools/repeat-control.py:27-28 '`--out` placed inside a tree the command itself inspects makes the command mismatch with itself; keep it outside that tree.'

The exact interface is accepted and executed: argv ['python3','tools/repeat-control.py','--runs','3','--out',DIR,'--','true'] -> `REPEAT_OUT <DIR>`, `REPEAT_CONTROL: controls_match`, exit=0; the `--` separator is mandatory (selftest case invalid-missing-separator PASS at invalid_usage/64). The /tmp example is illustrative; under the 2026-10-25 scratch directive the probes replaced DIR with an empty seat-scratch directory, which the tool accepts identically. Receipts: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt, selftest.txt.

findings.statement: retain raw observations before interpreting the finding.
findings.evidence: The tool saves, before printing its finding, run k's raw `stdout`, `stderr` and `exit` as DIR/run-<k>.{stdout,stderr,exit} plus command.txt and, written last, finding.txt (tools/repeat-control.py:20-26); the observed output dirs hold exactly those files (e.g. probe-findings/match.finding.txt contains `REPEAT_CONTROL: controls_match` / `REPEAT_EXIT: 0`). Receipts: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt, probe-findings/.

findings.statement: The output directory must not exist.
findings.evidence: argv ['python3','tools/repeat-control.py','--runs','3','--out',EXISTING_DIR,'--','true'] -> stderr `repeat-control: --out already exists (refused, never overwritten): <DIR>`, `REPEAT_CONTROL: invalid_usage`, exit=64; source uses `os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=False)` at tools/repeat-control.py:315. Receipt: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt.

findings.statement: Caller owns timeout policy; hanging commands yield no verdict.
findings.evidence: tools/repeat-control.py:84-88 'Limitations (stated, not hidden): there is no timeout and no process supervisor — a command that hangs yields no verdict'; the child call at :281-287 is subprocess.run with stdin/stdout/stderr set and no `timeout` keyword, and `grep -n 'timeout=\|alarm' tools/repeat-control.py` -> no match. Verified from source, not executed (a hang would only block).

findings.statement: Do not retry until green, normalize output, or interpret a finite match as proof of reliability.
findings.evidence: One pass, no retry branch: `for index in range(1, runs + 1)` at tools/repeat-control.py:325; byte-exact comparison with 'no decoding, stripping, newline normalization or whitespace folding' (:22-24); selftest cases `mismatch-newline-only` and `mismatch-run3-only` PASS at expected=controls_mismatch/1 (receipt selftest.txt:4-6), so a normalized or retried reading would be wrong. The finite-match bound is the tool's own text (:92-94). Receipt: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/selftest.txt.

findings.statement: Command stdout/stderr may contain sensitive data: choose a non-secret fixture command before retaining evidence.
findings.evidence: The tool retains raw command output with no redaction: bytes are written verbatim to run-<k>.stdout/.stderr (tools/repeat-control.py:20-26) and `grep -n 'redact\|sanitize\|scrub' tools/repeat-control.py` -> no match. The warning is therefore sound for any non-fixture command. Receipt: .ufo/waves/round-49/w1/T49SecR12.receipts/probes.txt.
